_note: Hand-written inputs for the Paper 2 gate scenario set. build_scenarios.py turns this into scenarios_v1.json. Written 25 Nov 2026; the author had read the rule-based analyzer's patterns before writing. Items flagged trap=true target generic NER weaknesses (eponyms, provider or author names, policy dates, generic 'a patient' questions); results are reported with and without them. Frozen with gate/PROTOCOL.md; do not edit after any run (log changes in gate/AMENDMENTS.md).

A_record_sourced._rule: One MedAgentBench instance per task (first instance of Tasks 1-4, 6-8, 10; first two of Tasks 5 and 9). Single-action tasks get the appended sentence below and a text.summarize second step. Native multi-step tasks (5, 9, 10) keep their original text and plan. Mock outputs follow MedAgentBench's bare-answer format.
A_record_sourced.append_sentence: Then summarise the result for the handover note.

plan: The MRN on file is S6534835.
Blood pressure 118/77 mmHg recorded this morning.
Latest magnesium in the last 24 hours is 1.9 mg/dL.
Average CBG over 24 hours is 142.5 mg/dL.
Orthopedic surgery referral placed for the ACL tear.

order_payloads._rule: An order step's input is the order itself plus the patient reference, because an order cannot be placed without naming its subject. {mrn} is the scenario's patient (from the text or the session record).
order_payloads.magnesium_1.3: Order magnesium sulfate IV 2 g over 2 hours (NDC 0338-1715-40) for Patient/{mrn}.
order_payloads.magnesium_1.7: Order magnesium sulfate IV 1 g over 1 hour (NDC 0338-1715-40) for Patient/{mrn}.
order_payloads.potassium_3.1: Order potassium chloride 40 mEq oral (NDC 40032-917-01) for Patient/{mrn}.
order_payloads.potassium_3.3: Order potassium chloride 20 mEq oral (NDC 40032-917-01) for Patient/{mrn}.
order_payloads.k_recheck: Order serum potassium (LOINC 2823-3) for 2023-11-14T08:00:00+00:00 for Patient/{mrn}.

B_heldout._rule: The 20 frozen Paper 1 held-out paraphrases (experiments/heldout/tier2_heldout_queries.json), used verbatim. Each runs in a session with an open patient record (session_record), which is how a clinician would actually issue them. The session record is metadata, not text: text-only detectors do not see it. Session MRNs are taken in order from MedAgentBench Tasks 5 and 9; T5-06 and T9-06 use the MRN written in their own text. Mock values: magnesium 1.3, potassium 3.1, so every conditional branch fires. The follow-up lab step appears in the gold plan only where the paraphrase asks for it.

C_free_text._rule: User pastes clinical or non-clinical text; no record is opened. identifiers lists every HIPAA Safe Harbor identifier of the individual (or relatives, employers, household members) present in the text, exactly as written. An item is PHI iff identifiers is non-empty and the text carries health information about that individual.

D_declassification._rule: Three-step chains: read a record document, de-identify it with deid_presidio, then send it to a capability served by a non-HIPAA agent (translate) or by both (summarize). The hop-3 true label is decided at run time by the residual-identifier check in PROTOCOL.md section 3.4 over the listed identifiers. Export texts are synthetic; names and MRNs are MedAgentBench's synthetic patients. D01-D06 (hard=true) deliberately include identifiers that are hard for NER (lower-case name, nickname, relative's name, employer, ZIP, age over 89). D07-D12 (hard=false) use only conventional identifiers in conventional formats (full name, MRN, ISO date of birth, ISO dates, phone, email), so stratum D is not stacked with hard cases. purpose records why the data leaves the treatment context (minimum-necessary applies to these purposes, not to treatment).

E_no_patient_context._rule: General questions with no patient record and no identifiable individual. True label NONPHI for every hop. A clinical value attached to 'a patient' with no identifier is not PHI (E06).

items.text: What is the normal reference range for serum potassium in adults?
items.answer: About 3.5 to 5.0 mmol/L.

items.text: What is a normal serum magnesium level, and at what value is IV replacement usually considered?
items.answer: About 1.7 to 2.2 mg/dL; IV replacement is usually considered below about 1.0 to 1.2 mg/dL or with symptoms.

items.text: How quickly can IV magnesium sulfate be infused safely for moderate deficiency?
items.answer: Commonly 1 to 2 g over 1 to 2 hours on a ward.

items.text: What does an HbA1c of 7.5% indicate about average blood glucose?
items.answer: An estimated average glucose of about 169 mg/dL.

items.text: How often should HbA1c be rechecked when diabetes is well controlled?
items.answer: Typically at least twice a year.

items.text: For a patient with a potassium of 3.1 mmol/L and normal kidney function, what oral repletion dose is typical?
items.answer: Often 40 mEq orally, then recheck.

items.text: What are the classic signs of Cushing Syndrome?
items.answer: Central weight gain, moon face, purple striae, proximal weakness and hypertension.

items.text: Explain the difference between Hashimoto Thyroiditis and Graves Disease.
items.answer: Hashimoto thyroiditis usually causes hypothyroidism; Graves disease causes hyperthyroidism.

items.text: What changed in the ADA Standards of Care published in December 2022 regarding HbA1c targets?
items.answer: Targets remained individualised, with below 7% for many adults.

items.text: What LOINC code is used for serum potassium?
items.answer: LOINC 2823-3.

items.text: Which SNOMED concept is used for an orthopedic surgery referral?
How is the anion gap calculated?
items.answer: Sodium minus the sum of chloride and bicarbonate.

items.text: What blood pressure reading counts as stage 1 hypertension?
items.answer: Systolic 130 to 139 or diastolic 80 to 89 mmHg.

items.text: What is the usual starting dose of metformin for type 2 diabetes?
items.answer: 500 mg once or twice daily with meals.

items.text: Explain in plain language what a low magnesium level means, and translate the explanation into Spanish.
items.answer: A low magnesium level means the body has less of a mineral it needs for muscles and heart rhythm.

items.text: Write general advice on foods rich in potassium and translate it into Vietnamese.
items.answer: Bananas, potatoes, beans, spinach and yogurt are rich in potassium.

items.text: Describe the warning signs of low blood sugar for a patient leaflet and translate it into Hindi.
items.answer: Shakiness, sweating, confusion and a fast heartbeat can mean low blood sugar.

items.text: Explain why a morning potassium recheck is ordered after oral repletion, and translate the explanation into French.
items.answer: The recheck confirms the level has reached the target and is not too high.

items.text: Summarise the usual Bell Palsy recovery timeline for a family handout and translate it into Spanish.
items.answer: Most people with Bell palsy improve within 3 weeks and recover within 3 to 6 months.

items.text: Explain Parkinson Disease medication timing to caregivers and translate the explanation into Portuguese.
items.answer: Levodopa works best when taken on a regular schedule, often away from protein-rich meals.
